title: CareSync POC scoping - quality eval plan
summary: POC scoping focused on quality evaluation for CareSync's clinical note generation use-case. Defined success criteria, workload sizing, baseline benchmarks, golden prompt set, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, scoring rubric, and timeline (3-week POC with benchmark runs). Next steps: share eval template, run baseline on hosted endpoint, provide sample dataset, schedule baseline benchmark run.
next_steps: Schedule baseline benchmark run w/ sample data (by 2026-01-22)
action_items: Lena Park - Send eval template and golden prompt examples - due 2026-01-18
Marco Chen - Export baseline perf checklist and security docs - due 2026-01-18
Alicia Gomez - Share anonymized 500 clinical notes + schema - due 2026-01-20
Sam Rodriguez - Confirm network/VPC constraints and permitted egress - due 2026-01-19
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-01-15 15:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Nair (CareSync Head of AI), Sam Rodriguez (CTO), Alicia Gomez (Clinical Data Lead)
transcript:
00:00 Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a minute, um hi priya, hi sam, hi alicia.
00:07 Priya (CareSync): Hi Lena, yeah thanks. we're excited to scope the POC, we've been looking at generative models to help summarize clinical visits into structured notes.
00:15 Marco (Redwood SE): Awesome. quick agenda — success criteria, workload sizing, baseline bench marks, and importantly the quality eval plan: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, scoring.
00:25 Sam (CareSync): Sounds good. we're mostly concerned about hallucinations and format correctness, also latency because this will be in clinician workflow.
00:35 Lena: Great, if we start with success criteria — what would success look like for the pilot? priya?
00:42 Priya: For us success is two-fold: 1) automated notes match clinician-entered gold standard 85% of the time on key fields (diagnosis, meds, follow up), 2) latency p95 under 800ms for single note generation, and 3) no high-severity hallucinations in sample of 500 notes.
00:58 Marco: Good, we'll capture that as target thresholds. we'll also measure token cost per note to estimate economics for Dedicated versus Hosted.
01:05 Alicia: On sample size, we can provide 500 anonymized visit notes spanning primary care and specialty, will that be enough?
01:12 Marco: That's a good starting point. for model selection and quality eval, 500 is workable: we'll split into 350 training-like prompts and 150 held-out for regression/acceptance testing.
01:22 Priya: timeline-wise, we want results in ~3 weeks; is that feasible?
01:28 Lena: Yes, typical POC timeline: week 1 onboarding + baseline runs, week 2 model tuning and eval, week 3 regression and handoff. so yeah ~3 weeks.
01:38 Marco: Now the quality eval plan specifics: we'll build a golden prompt set — canonical instructions clinicians use — and a ground-truth mapping for required slots. golden prompts will include negative tests and edge cases (missed meds, ambiguous timeline language).
01:52 Priya: Can you give an example golden prompt?
01:55 Marco: Sure — "Extract diagnosis list, current medications with dosages, and recommended follow-up actions from the clinical note. Output JSON with keys: diagnosis[], medications[{name,dose,frequency}], follow_up[]". We'll include format validators.
02:10 Sam: Format validators are key — if we require strict JSON we need schema enforcement; does Redwood support structured output validation?
02:16 Marco: Yes, we can run post-generation validators as part of the eval harness and count format failures as separate metric.
02:23 Lena: We'll also define hallucination checks: compare generated entities against note text and flag invented medications or dates not present; any invented critical facts count as high-severity.
02:33 Priya: How do you handle partial matches like abbreviations, e.g., "ASA" vs "aspirin"?
02:38 Marco: For that we normalize via clinical lexicon — we allow normalized matches; we'll capture normalization rules in the scoring rubric.
02:45 Marco: Scoring approach: composite score = weighted sum: correctness (50%), hallucination penalty (20%), format/adherence (15%), latency (10%), and cost per-note (5%).
02:57 Priya: weights make sense. can we tweak weights after baseline?
03:01 Lena: Absolutely, weights can be adjusted to align with your clinical risk tolerance.
03:05 Marco: Regression tests: we'll keep the 150 held-out golden prompts; after any model change we run regression and require no more than a 3 point absolute drop in composite score, and zero high-severity hallucination regressions.
03:18 Sam: About workload sizing, expected throughput — during peak clinician hours we expect 10 concurrent note generations, average 1.2 notes per clinician per hour, overall ~5k notes/day across org. does Redwood have guidance?
03:31 Marco: For 5k notes/day with bursts of 10 concurrent, we can start on Hosted with autoscaling. for production you'll likely want Dedicated if steady sustained throughput and lower unit costs. we'll include cost estimates in the follow-up.
03:44 Priya: Security — we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, all data residency in US, and optional customer-managed KMS. is Private deployment required?
03:53 Lena: For POC, Hosted with VPC peering and customer-managed keys is possible; Private becomes option if audits require it. we'll send our security pack.
04:03 Marco: Also we'll run a baseline benchmark: same 500 notes through chosen model variants (Redwood-curated open models + a quantized variant) to measure p50/p95 latency, token counts, and composite quality score.
04:16 Priya: Can you run both hosted endpoint and a local private sim so we can compare?
04:20 Marco: We can run hosted baseline; for private runtime we'd need Dedicated or Private deployment — we can simulate latency differences but can't run your on-prem hardware unless you host the runtime. we'll note that.
04:33 Lena: Let's talk deliverables: eval template + golden prompts, scoring rubric, security docs, benchmark plan, and timeline. we'll deliver the eval harness and a script to run baseline.
04:44 Priya: What's the acceptance criteria to move to a pilot/paid phase?
04:48 Lena: If composite score >= target (we'll document), p95 latency under your threshold (800ms), and no more than 0 high-sev hallucinations in held-out, we recommend moving to a pilot. also a cost estimate for monthly 5k notes.
05:02 Sam: ok thanks. any blockers on our side?
05:05 Alicia: we need to confirm data anonymization process and legal sign-off for sharing notes.
05:09 Marco: We can provide a template for anonymization and a checklist.
05:12 Lena: Next steps recap — we'll send eval template, security docs, and schedule baseline run for next week. follow-up meeting Monday 2026-01-26 to review baseline. everyone ok?
05:24 Priya: Sounds good.
05:26 Sam: yes.
05:27 Alicia: ok thanks.
05:29 Lena: Great, ending early. thanks everyone.
05:32 [call ends]

Notes: transcription has some minor errors (ASA / aspirin spelled out), and 'quantized variant' was sometimes transcribed as 'quantized variant' correctly; occasional filler words removed for readability.
Artifacts shared: Eval template: https://redwood.app/eval-template, Security pack: https://redwood.app/security/caresync
